title: Rabbi Reuven (a Palestinian Amora of the Third and Fourth Generations)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 11:7 he asked before Rabbi Mana (I), and in Midrash Tehillim 1:20 he spoke in Rabbi Chanina’s name.
At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 6: “Rabbi Reuven said: At that hour an angel came down and struck him on the mouth” (Nebuchadnezzar).

We find that he was expert in Greek, as in Petichta of Eichah, 31, and there 1:23. Of those who speak in his name we find Rabbi Bivi, as in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:1, who said: “The seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth.”
Rabbi Chilkiyah of the South in his name, as in Tanchuma, Kedoshim 1.
Rabbi Pinchas in his name, as in Tanchuma, Bereshit 18, and Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 75.
Rabbi Pinchas HaKohen in his name, as in Tanchuma, Toledot 11.

notes.text: The chapter/halakhah Shabbat and Sanhedrin references are Jerusalem Talmud. Saved Guggenheimer Shabbat6:9 and Sanhedrin1:1 contain the whole connected passages; the seal saying is Bivi in Reuven’s name.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:9 names Reuven in the angel narrative; Sanhedrin 1:1 explicitly has Bivi reporting Reuven on the divine seal. The Greek expertise, Mana-I placement and other cited midrashic transmissions remain Hyman’s account, not a new identity or chronology admission.
